This analysis loads the Ascl1-positive GBC object,
recalculates its resolution-0.7 marker genes, keeps the genes listed in
`ALL_TF`, selects the top eight TF markers per cluster, and plots the marker
heatmap. It then uses the existing PC1--5 tradeSeq fit to plot the same TF set
along pseudotime.

```{r setup, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
# Load packages used for the GBC, Slingshot, and tradeSeq plots.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  autodep = TRUE,
  cache.comments = FALSE,
  cache.path = file.path(
    here::here("results", "cache", "publication_pipeline"),
    paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(knitr::current_input())), "/")
  ),
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 6,
  dpi = 150
)

pipeline_root <- here::here()

# Load the saved inputs; tradeSeq is not refitted here.
ascl1_input_path <- file.path(params$download_dir, "gbc_subset.rds")
all_tf_path <- file.path(params$download_dir, "ALL_TF.Rda")
tradeseq_sce_path <- file.path(params$download_dir, "slingshot_output.rds")
tradeseq_fit_path <- file.path(params$download_dir, "tradeseq_fit_combined.rds")
figure_dir <- file.path(params$output_dir, "plots", "figure_4_ascl1_tf_tradeseq")

dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(tradeSeq)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(ggplot2)
})
```

## Load the Ascl1-positive cell object

Load the Ascl1-positive object and set the identity
classes to the same `RNA_snn_res.0.7` clusters used by the earlier scripts.

```{r load-ascl1-object}
# Load the GBC subset used for the Ascl1 transcription-factor heatmap.
ascl1_cells <- readRDS(ascl1_input_path)
DefaultAssay(ascl1_cells) <- "RNA"
Idents(ascl1_cells) <- "RNA_snn_res.0.7"

cluster_order <- c("1", "10", "0", "2", "4", "9", "11")
cluster_order <- cluster_order[
  cluster_order %in% as.character(unique(Idents(ascl1_cells)))
]

data.frame(
  cells = ncol(ascl1_cells),
  genes = nrow(ascl1_cells),
  clusters = paste(cluster_order, collapse = ", ")
)
```

## Calculate marker genes

Calculate positive cluster markers with the Seurat settings
used by the prior marker scripts: Wilcoxon testing, `min.pct = 0.1`, and
`logfc.threshold = 0.25`.

```{r calculate-marker-genes}
# Find markers for the GBC grouping used to rank transcription factors.
all_markers <- FindAllMarkers(
  ascl1_cells,
  only.pos = TRUE,
  min.pct = 0.1,
  logfc.threshold = 0.25,
  test.use = "wilcox",
  verbose = FALSE
)

all_markers$gene <- rownames(all_markers)
all_markers <- all_markers %>%
  mutate(
    cluster_id = as.character(cluster),
    pct.diff = pct.1 - pct.2
  ) %>%
  filter(cluster_id %in% cluster_order)

all_markers
```

## Load `ALL_TF` and subset the marker table

Load the `ALL_TF` reference and retain marker genes
that are present in that transcription-factor list.

```{r subset-tfs}
# Restrict the marker table to the transcription-factor list.
all_tf_environment <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
load(all_tf_path, envir = all_tf_environment)
ALL_TF <- unique(as.character(get("ALL_TF", envir = all_tf_environment)))

tf_markers <- all_markers %>%
  filter(gene %in% ALL_TF)

tf_markers
```

## Select the top eight TF markers per cluster

Rank TF markers by adjusted p value, then by fold change and
percent detected. It follows the earlier heatmap workflow by using average
RNA expression to assign a duplicated gene to the cluster where it is most
highly expressed.

```{r select-top-8}
# Select the eight highest-ranked transcription factors per GBC group.
ranked_tf_markers <- tf_markers %>%
  mutate(cluster_id = factor(cluster_id, levels = cluster_order)) %>%
  arrange(
    cluster_id,
    p_val_adj,
    desc(avg_log2FC),
    desc(pct.1),
    gene
  ) %>%
  group_by(cluster_id) %>%
  slice_head(n = 8) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(cluster_id = as.character(cluster_id))

average_expression <- AverageExpression(
  ascl1_cells,
  features = unique(ranked_tf_markers$gene),
  group.by = "RNA_snn_res.0.7",
  assays = "RNA",
  layer = "data",
  verbose = FALSE
)$RNA

colnames(average_expression) <- sub("^RNA\\.g", "", colnames(average_expression))
colnames(average_expression) <- sub("^RNA\\.", "", colnames(average_expression))
colnames(average_expression) <- sub("^g", "", colnames(average_expression))

average_expression_long <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(average_expression)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -gene,
    names_to = "cluster_id",
    values_to = "assign_avg"
  )

top8_tf <- ranked_tf_markers %>%
  left_join(
    average_expression_long,
    by = c("gene", "cluster_id")
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(assign_avg),
    p_val_adj,
    desc(avg_log2FC),
    desc(pct.1),
    gene
  ) %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(cluster_id = factor(cluster_id, levels = cluster_order)) %>%
  arrange(cluster_id, p_val_adj, desc(avg_log2FC), desc(pct.1), gene) %>%
  mutate(
    global_row_order = row_number(),
    gene_label = gene
  )

top8_tf
```

## Plot the Ascl1-positive TF heatmap

Scale each gene across clusters and plot the selected top-eight
TF markers in cluster order.

```{r ascl1-tf-heatmap, cache=FALSE}
# Build and print the heatmap with the published ordering, labels, and scales.
heatmap_data <- average_expression_long %>%
  filter(cluster_id %in% cluster_order) %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  mutate(
    z_expr = ifelse(
      is.na(sd(assign_avg)) || sd(assign_avg) == 0,
      0,
      (assign_avg - mean(assign_avg)) / sd(assign_avg)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  inner_join(
    top8_tf %>% select(gene, gene_label, global_row_order),
    by = "gene"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cluster_id = factor(cluster_id, levels = cluster_order),
    gene_label = factor(
      gene_label,
      levels = rev(top8_tf %>% arrange(global_row_order) %>% pull(gene_label))
    )
  )

ascl1_tf_heatmap <- ggplot(
  heatmap_data,
  aes(x = cluster_id, y = gene_label, fill = z_expr)
) +
  geom_tile(color = NA, linewidth = 0) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#f1eef6",
    mid = "#9e9ac8",
    high = "#54278f",
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Scaled\navg expr"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold", size = 8.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic", size = 7.2),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.32, "in"),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 5.5, 5.5)
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(figure_dir, "ascl1_res07_top8_unique_tf_heatmap.png"),
  ascl1_tf_heatmap,
  width = 3.8,
  height = 5.35,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

ggsave(
  file.path(figure_dir, "ascl1_res07_top8_unique_tf_heatmap.pdf"),
  ascl1_tf_heatmap,
  width = 3.8,
  height = 5.35,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)

write.csv(
  top8_tf,
  file.path(figure_dir, "ascl1_top8_tf_markers.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

ascl1_tf_heatmap
```

## Load the existing PC1--5 tradeSeq fit

Load the fitted Slingshot SCE and combined tradeSeq GAM fit
used for the PC1--5 trajectory. It does not refit tradeSeq.

```{r load-tradeseq-fit}
# Load the tradeSeq fit and Slingshot object.
sce_tradeseq <- readRDS(tradeseq_sce_path)
gam_fit <- readRDS(tradeseq_fit_path)

tradeSeq_genes <- intersect(unique(top8_tf$gene), rownames(gam_fit))
tradeSeq_genes <- intersect(tradeSeq_genes, rownames(sce_tradeseq))

if (length(tradeSeq_genes) == 0) {
  stop("None of the selected top-eight TF markers are present in the tradeSeq fit.")
}

tradeSeq_genes
```

## Predict tradeSeq expression along pseudotime

Calculate the fitted expression curves for the selected TFs along
each Slingshot lineage.

```{r predict-tradeseq}
# Predict expression for the selected genes along each lineage.
tradeSeq_predictions <- tradeSeq::predictSmooth(
  gam_fit,
  gene = tradeSeq_genes,
  nPoints = 200,
  tidy = TRUE
)

lineage_labels <- c(
  "1" = "OSN",
  "2" = "Sus",
  "3" = "HBC",
  "4" = "MV"
)

tradeSeq_predictions <- tradeSeq_predictions %>%
  mutate(
    lineage_id = as.character(lineage),
    lineage = factor(
      unname(lineage_labels[lineage_id]),
      levels = c("OSN", "Sus", "HBC", "MV")
    )
  )
```

## Plot the tradeSeq curves

Plot fitted TF expression curves across pseudotime, with one
facet per selected TF and one colored curve for each lineage.

```{r tradeseq-plot, cache=FALSE}
# Build and print the smoother plot with the published mappings, labels, and scales.
lineage_colors <- c(
  "OSN" = "#6A1B9A",
  "Sus" = "#1F78B4",
  "HBC" = "#009E73",
  "MV" = "#D95F02"
)

tradeseq_tf_plot <- ggplot(
  tradeSeq_predictions,
  aes(x = time, y = yhat, color = lineage, group = lineage)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~gene, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = lineage_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Pseudotime",
    y = "tradeSeq fitted expression",
    color = "Lineage"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "italic", size = 8),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.7, "lines")
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(figure_dir, "ascl1_top8_tf_tradeseq_smoothers.png"),
  tradeseq_tf_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 10,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

ggsave(
  file.path(figure_dir, "ascl1_top8_tf_tradeseq_smoothers.pdf"),
  tradeseq_tf_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 10,
  units = "in",
  bg = "white"
)

tradeseq_tf_plot
```
